subject: design-technology
title: User-Centred Design
welcome_lead: Designing for people, not just yourself.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: user-centred design, target audience, empathy.
final_note: Find out what users actually need before you design.

concepts.def: Person who will use the product.
Short statement of what is needed.

walkthroughs.body_html: Designers begin by asking: who is this? A 5-year-old and a 75-year-old need different things. The target audience guides every choice.
A persona is a made-up but realistic user — age, hobbies, problems. Designing for 'Asha, 12, plays football, loves bright colours' is sharper than for 'a child'.
A brief is the project starting point: what to make, for whom, by when, budget. From it you write a detailed specification — measurements, materials, features.
